summary: Streaming chat sessions disconnect or stall mid-generation for users on intermittent mobile networks
description: Issue summary: Multiple customers (notably ByteFlow Analytics) report that SSE/WebSocket-based streaming chat responses either disconnect abruptly or stall indefinitely during mid-generation when the user is on spotty mobile networks. Impact: Partial responses are being delivered, the finalization event ("response.complete") is missing in many cases leading to client-side timeouts and retries. Several customers report increased error rates starting after the 2026-03-12 midnight UTC deploy to streaming-proxy. Environment: Production (us-west primary), affected across us-west and eu-central customers, primarily on circuits with high jitter and intermittent packet loss.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the hosted chat API with streaming enabled (SSE or WebSocket) and model=redwood-chat-1.
2) Simulate an intermittent mobile network (high jitter, small packet loss) using network throttling (e.g., tc/netem or a mobile device with flaky signal).
3) Send a multi-paragraph prompt that triggers multi-chunk streaming (> 3 chunks).
4) Observe connection behavior and whether 'response.complete' or final event is received by client within expected timeframe.
observed_behavior: Clients report connections either dropping with upstream errors (502/504) or streams freezing with no new events for >30s while server-side logs show partial chunk writes. In some cases the client eventually reconnects and receives duplicated tokens from server-side retries.
expected_behavior: Streaming connections should deliver all chunks followed by a final completion event. On transient network blips the server should keep the stream alive long enough for client reconnection or gracefully terminate with a clear error so client can retry deterministically.

investigation_notes: Initial correlation with 2026-03-12 deploy of streaming-proxy (PR #88) which adjusted keepalive and write timeout heuristics.
Reproduced locally by introducing 200-400ms jitter + 1-2% packet loss; observed same stall pattern where last chunk and completion event not flushed.
Hypothesis 1: aggressive upstream write timeouts in streaming-proxy close connection before kernel buffers are flushed under high jitter.

Hypothesis 2: batching/continuous-inference change in runtime (runtime PR #459) increased chunking frequency; combined with proxy change this results in more small writes causing buffer coalescing issues.
SRE ran an A/B with streaming-proxy rollback -> client reports decreased disconnects on test cohort.
No evidence of model runtime OOMs; GPU metrics stable.

2026-03-13 14:27 - Elena Cruz (SRE): Captured tcpdump; saw FIN from streaming-proxy shortly after small write. Suspect proxy write timeout config is closing streams on backpressure.
2026-03-13 15:10 - Ravi Desai (Runtime Eng): Confirmed PR #459 changed flush thresholds; will test combining revert of small-write flush and proxy keepalive tweak.

2026-03-13 16:40 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer ByteFlow confirmed decreased failures after mitigation applied to test cohort (rollback proxy config). Customer requested follow-up and permanent fix timeline.
workarounds: 1) Temporary: Rolled back streaming-proxy keepalive/write-timeout changes for affected nodes (rolled to previous stable tag) which reduced disconnects for test customers.
2) Client-side: Recommend clients implement idempotent request IDs and resume logic that can handle replays (server currently does best-effort dedup for short windows).
3) For dedicated customers: advised to pin to a non-chunking config as short-term measure, if acceptable.
resolution: Mitigation applied: reverted streaming-proxy timeout changes and applied a conservative keepalive for mobile-region edge pools. Runtime team opened follow-up PR to batch-flush less aggressively (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/472). Monitoring alerts added for 'streaming_partial_finalize' and a synthetic mobile-net connectivity test. Next steps: coordinate a staged rollout of runtime PR, add end-to-end tests for intermittent networks, and schedule postmortem after full remediation.
next_steps: 1) Runtime team to land PR #472 and run canary for 48h.
2) SRE to instrument streaming success-rate by client-network-type and promote synthetic test to CI.
3) CS to notify impacted customers with ETA and postmortem link.
